page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with x86_64 architecture, offering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server configuration includes a 262 GB local SSD and is Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-performance disk attachments. It does not feature any dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on the AMD EPYC processor for computational tasks.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core tests, and strong memory performance via PassMark memory scores. Image processing workloads and small-model LLM text generation also show strong performance. Most other metrics, including multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, database operations, and web serving throughput, fall into the average performance tier. However, the server exhibits weak performance when processing prompts for large 70B LLM models, highlighting a limitation for heavy AI workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32as_v4 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose enterprise workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. It is well-suited for applications such as web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate image processing tasks.
